revisions.original: 20 outer posts with no stated plan
revisions.revised: posts at equal 18° steps on an ellipse with semi-axes 33 × 25, offset half a step so the −z axis falls between two posts
revisions.reason: the 72 × 56 envelope includes the 6 m footings; equal angles keep lintel spans 8.4–10.6 m
revisions.impact: the main opening on −z is a lintel bay of 10.6 m clear between post faces; a 12 m route uses the wider gap at the horseshoe's open end (see entries)

revisions.original: six rows × eight columns, ≥16 m clear between the central rows
revisions.reason: central high columns at x = ±11.5 leave 23 − 2 × 2.5 = 18 m clear for the central passage; outer columns keep the 144 m envelope with 6 m overhangs of roof
revisions.impact: the central passage runs along z through all six rows

revisions.original: three 2 m construction bands
revisions.revised: front and rear flights of 24 risers of 0.25 m and 1.5 m treads, 24 m wide
revisions.reason: a 2 m band is a construction band, not a stair riser (§7.2)
revisions.impact: approaches extend 36 m beyond the 184 m envelope; the core bounds stay within it

revisions.original: 34–38 m capitals: six expanding rings of 32 D each, then three 6 m square abacus layers R(6,6,1,1)
revisions.revised: each echinus course is a solid cushion band: its 32-segment outer ring stacked at the D section to fill the 0.42 m course plus one ring just inside it (the underside of the overhang); each abacus layer keeps its R(6,6,1,1) frame stacked to the 0.5 m layer; the core behind is the capital shade shell (inner rings and abacus decks hidden by the band, the next course and the architrave were removed 2026-11-04: 1,963 → 997 D per capital)
revisions.reason: single 0.125 m rings 0.42 m apart and hollow square frames read as a see-through wire lampshade in the real viewport, failing Appendix C2 (capitals must cast readable shadows; outward-flaring support below a square abacus)
revisions.impact: same 4 m capital height and 6 m abacus width (envelope unchanged); more D pieces per column (BOM); the capital reads as an echinus cushion under a solid slab and shadows the frieze

revisions.original: 20 B outer ribs per segment
revisions.revised: 20 M ribs per segment (0.5 m fillets)
revisions.reason: twenty 1 m-wide B sections need 20 m of perimeter; a Ø 5.2 m shaft has 16.3 m, so B ribs would overlap into a smooth cylinder and leave no room for the flutes
revisions.impact: same count and rhythm, true recessed flutes between ribs; the BOM shows M instead of B

revisions.original: six expanding rings and three R(6,6,1,1) abacus layers in 34–38 m
revisions.revised: six 32-D echinus rings at 0.42 m spacing and three D R(6,6) abacus frames at 0.5 m spacing, capital top 37.06 m
revisions.reason: the rings and frames resolve to 3.06 m; a 0.94 m M bearing course closes to 38 m
revisions.impact: the entablature still spans 38–44 m

revisions.original: main hall 72 × 80, side porch 32 × 48, 12 m terrace
revisions.revised: main platform 80 × 128 (hall 72 × 80 colonnade on it, the rest an open court), side platform 36 × 56 holding the 32 × 48 porch; a 12 m-wide flight links the 4 m and 8 m levels
revisions.reason: 112 × 128 envelope: 80 + 36 = 116 overlaps 4 m where the side terrace tucks under the main platform's edge
revisions.impact: the court in front of the hall is the 'open connecting court'

revisions.original: legacy B4: 224 M + 1,400 D per column (paper)
revisions.revised: B4 generated: actual per-column counts in the BOM (base, shaft, neck, flare, volutes, abacus)
revisions.reason: B4's counts were never generated; the generator expands the same rings, ribs and spirals and reports what it actually placed
revisions.impact: see the generated BOM; the 3,306-piece offline sample is not used

revisions.original: approximately 180 m
revisions.revised: 188 m (six 22 m openings, seven 8 m piers)
revisions.reason: openings and piers resolved at their stated sizes
revisions.impact: the lower tier is 8 m longer than the round figure

revisions.original: 12 piers, roughly 20 m clear spans, not over lower arch centres
revisions.revised: twelve 6.67 m piers at a 26.67 m pitch; piers over the lower tier stand on its deck beam, the outer five per side on the bank terrace
revisions.reason: an exact 1:1 pier alignment with the lower tier (30 m pitch) is impossible with 11 arches over 300 m; every middle pier over the 188 m lower tier lands on the 2 m lower beam band, none over an arch crown's keystone (checked: min distance from a lower crown ≥ 3.3 m)
revisions.impact: the middle tier reads as its own rhythm, as at the reference

revisions.original: 20 m deep envelope; 4 m channel plus ≥ 4 m walk
revisions.revised: lower tier 20 m, middle 16 m, top 8 m plus a 7.5 m cantilevered walk deck to z = 9.75 (bracketed on the upper beam)
revisions.reason: a stepped section keeps the tiers distinct and the walk wide enough to land on
revisions.impact: the channel is 4 m wide between M walls; the walk is 7.5 m

revisions.original: ellipse 240 × 196; four steps
revisions.revised: step ellipses 240 × 196 at the base, shrinking 0.8 m per band; pier axes on a 226 × 182 ellipse so the attached half-columns stay within the envelope
revisions.reason: the envelope includes the stepped base and the projecting half-columns
revisions.impact: the steps are a walkable 0.5 m-riser plinth; entries cross it on ramps

revisions.original: rotunda outside Ø 96, overall depth 144, envelope width 112
revisions.revised: drum Ø 96 centred at z = +16; six base bands step out to Ø 112; portico from z = −72 to the drum
revisions.reason: the 112 m width is the stepped base, the 144 m depth is base + portico
revisions.impact: none on the dome

revisions.original: 16 × 5 D leaf groups and three abacus layers
revisions.revised: two rows of eight clusters (16) of five D leaf lanes, each lane bent in two (lower row) or four (upper row) D runs so the cluster widens, closes to a point and turns its tip down; three stepped abacus frames
revisions.reason: with one run per lane the five lanes of a cluster fell on the same line; the builder dropped four of five as coincident duplicates, leaving 32 single sticks per capital that read as loose wires (inspector review 2026-11-04); the brief asks for broad, opening, pointed clusters
revisions.impact: 240 leaf D per capital instead of the 32 that survived (+3,328 pieces over the sixteen portico columns)

revisions.original: approximately 56 m span, 24 m rise, A(56,24,3,8,4), 42–66
revisions.revised: clear span 64 − 0 between pier inner faces = 64 m at 44 → resolved as A(64, 24, 3, 8, 4) springing at 42 + 2 = 44 on a 2 m pier cap, crown 68 + 3
revisions.reason: the piers' inner faces stand 64 m apart (the retained central space); a 56 m arch would not land on them
revisions.impact: pendentives fill the spandrels between the crowns at 68; the drum sits on 68–76

revisions.original: eight outer towers, eight polyline wall runs
revisions.revised: towers at the four corners (to 72 m) and the four side midpoints (to 64 m) of a 160 × 136 polygon; tower radius 6 m, conical roofs radius 7
revisions.reason: corner towers carry the tallest roofs; runs between towers are the eight wall runs
revisions.impact: the main gate is beside the south tower, offset from the inner gate

revisions.original: 8 B vertical bundle members + 8 M ring ties per 4 m course
revisions.revised: 8 B members lapping two courses each (one set per two courses) + 8 M ties every course
revisions.reason: 8 m B stock spans two 4 m courses; placing a new set every course would double each member
revisions.impact: BOM: 5 × 8 B per pier rather than 10 × 8

revisions.original: maintenance-display opening
revisions.revised: the outer shell's plank infill is omitted on the octagon's −z lobe between rings 8 and 16, showing the inner shell and ties
revisions.reason: an honest reveal without a new visitor route through the 2 m cavity
revisions.impact: visible from the hall roof and from flight

revisions.original: two wings of 16 arc positions × four radial rows (128 columns)
revisions.revised: wings on circles of radius 118/122/126/130 m around (0, −16), each over 66° of arc centred on ±x; the wing bases reach ±140 m (280 m); two paved forecourt bands mark the square's front at z = −120; the facade base reaches z = +120
revisions.reason: fits the 280 m width with the facade and dome on +z inside the 240 m depth
revisions.impact: the main approach crosses the open square between the wing ends

revisions.original: nine bays with the middle three wider
revisions.revised: bay lines at x = ±70/±56/±42/±28/±12: six outer bays of 14 m and three middle bays of 16/24/16 m
revisions.reason: a 16 m main entrance clearance needs the central bay ≥ 16 m between column chains
revisions.impact: the main door is 18 m clear

revisions.original: nominally 21 × 11 nodes; list nodes removed for the central passage
revisions.revised: removed: nodes (i = 9…11, j = 4…6) under the transept vault, replaced by the vault's 56 m arches; nodes (i = 0 and 20, j = 4…6) at both ends, leaving 48 m entrances (≥ 32 m)
revisions.reason: the passage and the transept need clear floor
revisions.impact: 231 − 15 = 216 columns

revisions.original: 100 × 100 envelope, four 18 m pads, leg centre radius 42 at the base
revisions.revised: the leg centre radius 42/39/35/30/25/20/16 is measured from each vertical mid-plane (|x| = |z| = r); pads 18 × 18 centred at |x| = |z| = 41; the 12 m leg section at r = 42 reaches ±48, pads ±50
revisions.reason: read as a diagonal distance the legs would stand only 30 m off-axis and the tower would be 75 m wide, not 100
revisions.impact: the legs spread wider, so the lower arches span about 60 m between leg faces

revisions.original: nominal plan 56 × 40, retreat 2 m every four floors
revisions.revised: floors 29–32 at 56 × 40, 33–36 at 52 × 36, 37–40 at 48 × 32 (2 m off every face), each setback a 2 m terrace inside a 4 m-wide roof edge with rails
revisions.reason: a symmetric 2 m retreat on each face per stage
revisions.impact: three principal setbacks at 40, 120 and 168, plus two minor ones

revisions.original: 360 × 160 envelope, curved upstream plan, 36 bands × 36 arc sectors
revisions.revised: upstream face on a 260 m radius (convex toward the reservoir at −z), crest arc x = ±170; the canyon narrows the body to ±60 m at the foundation; thickness by Catmull-Rom through 110/82/52/27/12 m; 36 equal-angle sectors per band, trimmed by the canyon
revisions.reason: a dam fills a V-shaped canyon: full-width sectors at the base would hang in the rock
revisions.impact: the 160 m depth = 110 m base thickness + the plan sagitta + spillway toe; the crest is 12 m thick

revisions.original: §7.4 local sample: 61.75 m high, back at z = −6
revisions.revised: used unchanged as a lower downstream annex at the crown, its origin at the dam toe (back bedded into the body), between the two powerhouses, discharging into the central channel
revisions.reason: keeps the 160 m dam and adds the required fins, bays, bottom-wide/top-narrow sections and spreading chute faces
revisions.impact: the spillway reads from the toe and from the crest road above

revisions.original: 20 column bundles on the 6 × 4 grid perimeter, 16 m central passage
revisions.revised: the two bundles on the passage line (x = 0, z = ±24) move sideways to x = ±8 on their facades, so the passage along z is 16 m clear between them
revisions.reason: a bundle on the passage axis would block it
revisions.impact: same 20 bundles; the facade bays beside the passage are 8 and 4 m

revisions.original: 8 m-wide edge-viewing terraces around 76, 140 and 204 m, projecting 4 m
revisions.revised: on floors 16, 32 and 48 (floor f's slab at 12 + 4(f − 1) = 72, 136, 200 m): a ring 8 m wide whose outer 4 m cantilevers beyond the facade on bracket groups every 8 m; the inner 4 m is the recessed floor edge
revisions.reason: floor and elevation conventions resolved (floor 1 at 12 m)
revisions.impact: the terraces reach the 80 × 56 envelope

revisions.original: A and I end at 30; C and G at 42; D/F/H at 54; B/E continue to 60
revisions.revised: as written; tube E (centre) is full height; B shares E's west… north face and continues beside it
revisions.reason: unchanged
revisions.impact: from above: nine → seven → cross of five → two

revisions.original: four right-triangle zones around the centre, ending at floors 40/48/56/64
revisions.revised: the 88 m square split by both diagonals into four isosceles right triangles W/S/N/E ending at floors 40/48/56/64; each part's crown slopes down toward the lower neighbour's side over its last four floors
revisions.reason: the diagonals give one shared central edge (assigned once, to the last-ending prism E)
revisions.impact: the 12 m diagonal route at the base runs from SW to NE between the W/S and N/E pairs

revisions.original: each wing: double-M mullions every 4 m along both sides, a 12-segment nose and M floor-edge ring
revisions.revised: the double-M mullions also stand at the nose's eleven interior segment points (0.3 m outside the outline, as on the sides), and the nose carries glass strips tangent to each segment
revisions.reason: with mullions only on the straight sides, the three rounded noses showed the dark wing interior as bare 300 m slabs (inspector review, 2026-11-04)
revisions.impact: the curtain wall reads continuously round each wing; more M pieces (BOM); envelope unchanged

revisions.original: rear shading shells behind the curtain wall (§7.2: allowed)
revisions.revised: the wing-prism and core infill shells use the plank finish (lit timber tone) instead of the near-black shade finish
revisions.reason: about 54,000 m² of shade behind 38 %-opaque glass made the whole tower read as a black slab from every review camera, hiding the setbacks and terraces (inspector review, 2026-11-04); L18/L19 show timber behind their glass
revisions.impact: appearance only; no piece, collider or envelope change

revisions.original: wings initially about 56 m long and 24 m wide at 120°, envelope 144 × 132; each wing retreats four times 56 → 48 → 40 → 32 → 24
revisions.revised: wings 81 m from the core centre to the nose tip (65 m beyond the 16 m core), retreating 8 m at each of its four setbacks: 81 → 73 → 65 → 57 → 49
revisions.reason: with 56 m wings the Y plan's bounding box is only 100 × 90; 81 m wings meet 144 × 132 (solved numerically from the outline); the 8 m step per setback is kept
revisions.impact: the final wing stubs are longer than 24 m, so the crown's wing fins carry the sequence's end
